description.narrative:
The objective of the proposed program is to improve the lives of people living in poverty through expanding access to renewable energy and clean cooking technologies in mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar to assure health andenvironmental sustainability. Below are selected outcome and impact indicators from ESMAPs Results Framework and Theory of Change.
Crosscutting impact indicators (to measure the TOC development objectives): - Generation Capacity of Renewable Energy Expected to be installed (utility scale and distributed resources), and Metric Tons of CO2 Emissions expected to b reduced per year.
Outcome indicators: - Renewable Energy and Climate Change: Government adopts policies and plans to support major scaleup of renewable energy. Stimulation of public and private investment in Renewable Energy and ancillary infrastructure - Energy Efficiency and Demand Side Management: Government adopts policies and plans to accelerate Energy Efficiency - Clean Cooking: Improvement in the enabling environment for clean cooking - Gender and Productive Uses of Electricity: Increased share of female employees, leaders, entrepreneurs and consumers in the energy sector.
The importance of Embassy to contribute to ESMAPWB Trust Funds: Trust funds enable financial, knowledge, and other forms of collaboration among Development Partners, client countries, and other stakeholders, at the country level. Development Partners work with the World Bank through Trust Funds for the following reasons: - To align and catalyze scaledup funding support with other Development Partners within agreed strategic frameworks, including for global public goods - To leverage the World Banks convening power, at the country level, to maximize coordinated action and achieve impact at scale - To benefit from the World Banks extensive technical expertise, country experience and supervision capacity, its financial control framework, and its ability to monitor and report on results - To support innovative or emerging policy areas, which the Embassy view as apriority.

Världsbankens Trust Fund via dess Energy Sector Management Assistance Programme (ESMAP) för 3-årsperioden 2022-2025 med ett bidrag på 22 MSEK. Det föreslagna programmet syftar till att förbättra fattiga människors levnadsförhållanden genom utökad tillgång till förnybar energi och teknik för ren matlagning på det Tanzaniska fastlandet samt på Zanzibar.

World Bank Trust Fund through Energy Sector Management Assistance Program (ESMAP) with a contribution of SEK 22 million for the next three years 2022 - 2025. The proposed program aims to improve the lives of people living in poverty through expanding access to renewable energy and clean cooking technologies in mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar.

description.narrative:
Progress on Results/Activities April 2024-November 2025: Activities supported during the April 2024 to November 2025 period, the focus of the TF activities supported Tanzania Rural Electrification Expansion Program (TREEP) and Zanzibar Energy Sector Transformation and Access Project (ZESTA) implementation during this period and included the following:
(i) Renewable Energy (RE), Climate Change: under this thematic area ESMAP has assisted EWURA in developing, appraising and supervising (SPP) renewable energy projects in the country on rules, guidelines and standardized documents that form the regulatory foundation. Further the Sida funding has ensured implementation of RE projects under Tanzania Energy Development and Access Expansion Project (TEDAP) and Tanzania Rural Electrification Expansion Program (TREEP). Regarding TEDAP 25,45 MW was installed through six projects (exceeding set target of 47 percent). Over the years 2024- 2025 TANESCO has signed 22 Standard Power Purchase Agreements (SPPAs) powered by Solar and Hydro resources. Three of these have received loans for around 13 Million USD. The Zanzibar Energy Sector Transformation and Access Project (ZESTA) will finance a 18 MW grid connected solar PV plant. The ESMAP team (TZA) provided technical assistance to Tanzanias CCDR (Tanzanias Country Climate Development Report) finalized in December 2024 and to the national strategy for Renewable Energy. The provided support will contribute and feed into Tanzania´s climate commitments and the NDC implementation. The team has commenced a grid stability analysis to be finalized in March 2026.
(ii) Energy Efficiency and Demand Side Management: The team is working on Productive Use of Energy and Electricity (PUE) together with the World Bank´s Agriculture and Water Global Practises to scale up solar water pumping. especially prioritizing micro and small enterprises (MSMEs) as analysis of the PUE ecosystem.
(iii) Clean Cooking under the TREEP AF, the Bank is supporting the procurement by MOE of a Clean Cooking Baseline study. The study will serve as a benchmark for assessing and promoting the transition to cleaner and more sustainable cooking solutions in the country. Continuosly support for accelerating access to clean cooking through policy advice, technical analysis, and capacity building. The ESMAP clean cooking team will give support on investment opportunities in coordination with the donors. Baseline data and information collected will be the basis for directing and guiding the implementation of the National Clean Cooking Strategy. Through SIDA support the Bank provided technical experts who have been able to provide critical insights into the design of the TOR for this activity.
(iv) Gender and Productive Uses of Electricity: Under the TREEP AF, the Bank under Sida funding is providing technical expert support to Rural Energy Agency (REA) in development of gender situational analysis, REA Gender Mainstreaming policy, in alignment with the REA Gender Strategy and REA Gender Plan
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
